audits.title: 472 An Audit on the Optimal Timing of Imaging in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.standard: IAP/APA and BSG guidance: diagnosis within 48 hours, ultrasound within 24 hours of diagnosis, CT at 72-96 hours after onset or after 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 90%; CT after 48 hours of admission 6.15%; CT within 72-96 hours of onset 29.23%; ultrasound within 24 hours 17%; CT initial imaging in 75%.

audits.other_findings: Staff education and increased ultrasound availability suggested.
audits.citation: Patel M, Khawaja A, Oki T, Eigbefoh R, De Silva K, More A, et al.. 472 An Audit on the Optimal Timing of Imaging in Acute Pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.107.

audits.title: OGBN P12 Use of Computed Tomographic Scan in Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pancreatitis; A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Local policy on CT use in acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: NHS hospital in North West England (Salford Royal Hospital)

cycle1.result: 42 (79.2%) had CT; 12 (28.5%) of scans considered unnecessary.

audits.other_findings: 42.9% of scans were in patients without diagnostic amylase.
audits.citation: Moti T, Alwani O, Baltatzis M, Alasmar M. OGBN P12 Use of Computed Tomographic Scan in Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pancreatitis; A Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad348.105.

audits.title: 686 National Audit Assessing the Imaging of Acute Pancreatitis at Mater Dei Hospital, Malta
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists recommendations: CT at least 72 hours after symptom onset, prognostic factors in report, gallbladder US within 24 hours

cycle1.result: Of 99 CTs, 25.3% at least 72 hours after symptoms; 24.2% reported all 3 prognostic factors; 20.2% had gallbladder US within 24 hours.

audits.intervention: Planned educational sessions for emergency doctors, surgeons and radiologists.
audits.other_findings: 47.3% of those with early CT had further CT or MRCP in the same admission.
audits.citation: Formosa D, Catania S, Caruana C. 686 National Audit Assessing the Imaging of Acute Pancreatitis at Mater Dei Hospital, Malta. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.256.

audits.title: 353 Re-Audit on the Utilization of CT Scans in Acute Pancreatitis Management Following Implementation of Local Policy in a Northwest NHS Hospital
audits.standard: Local hospital policy on CT imaging in acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: Emergency surgical team, Salford Royal Hospital (Northwest NHS hospital)

cycle1.result: 28% of CT scans for acute pancreatitis were unnecessary.

audits.intervention: Targeted education and retraining of staff on the local imaging policy.

cycle2.result: CT in 23 patients (71.8%); only 1 scan (4.3%) unnecessary, 95.6% compliance with imaging policy.

audits.other_findings: 15 (46.1%) CTs done in patients without diagnostic amylase levels, 3 after 72 hours for complications.
audits.citation: Alwani O, Moti T, Baltatzis M, Alasmar M. 353 Re-Audit on the Utilization of CT Scans in Acute Pancreatitis Management Following Implementation of Local Policy in a Northwest NHS Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_17). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf270.131.

audits.title: Optimizing Imaging Adherence in Acute Pancreatitis: A Clinical Audit at a District General Hospital.
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists imaging standards for acute pancreatitis (no routine early CT without severe features)
audits.setting: District general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust, A&E presentations

cycle1.result: 24 (54%) had CT, 15 of them within 72 hours; serum amylase checked in all; ultrasound within 24 hours infrequent.

audits.intervention: Departmental presentations and posters to raise awareness of imaging guidelines.

cycle2.result: 15 (46.8%) had CT, three within 72 hours; serum amylase checked in all.

audits.other_findings: Imaging findings were consistent with pancreatitis in 80% of cycle 1 scans.
audits.citation: Pal S, Oxenham M, Chand M, Allu J. Optimizing Imaging Adherence in Acute Pancreatitis: A Clinical Audit at a District General Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e94967. doi:10.7759/cureus.94967. PMID: 41122368.
